Australia is the ((++largest smallest)) country in Oceania, covering more than 85% of the continent by area.

hint.label: Imaginary lines
hint.text: The Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn are imaginary lines circling the Earth. The Equator is in the middle and divides the globe into its Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Tropic of Capricorn is located just south of the Equator.

atoms.text: Oceania lies mainly in the Southern Hemisphere, with just a few island nations in the Northern Hemisphere. Because of its vast area, Oceania has many different climates.
Most Pacific islands lie near the Equator. This means they are tropical and have warm temperatures, high humidity and distinct wet and dry seasons.
Northern Australia remains tropical. However, further south, Australia’s huge interior has a dry climate. Here you can find deserts with little rainfall and extreme temperatures.
New Zealand has a mainly temperate climate with regular rainfall and mild temperatures. The surrounding Pacific Ocean also helps prevent extreme heat or cold.

atoms.b: Many countries in Oceania belong to the Commonwealth of Nations. The ((++countries oceans)) in this group share common goals and values, but each member state still makes its own laws and political decisions.
Most Commonwealth nations were once part of the British Empire. Australia and New Zealand, for example, still feature the Union ((++Jack Crown)) on their flags, showing these historic ties.
Member states also ((++gather separate)) for the Commonwealth Games to compete in a range of sports. This international event is held every four years in a different city.
